### NEW in 2026 (b) — Managed Agents **memory stores** (server-side memory, this is the big one)

This is a genuinely new *server-side* memory product distinct from the client-side `memory_20250818` tool, and it's the most directly relevant prior art for a MongoDB-backed knowledge layer.

- Public beta **April 23, 2026** under `managed-agents-2026-04-01`; memory-store endpoints later moved to their own beta header **`agent-memory-2026-07-22`** (July 2, 2026). Sending both headers on a memory-store request returns **400**. [VERIFIED from source: https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/release-notes/api and https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/memory]
- Model: a **memory store** (`memstore_...`) is a workspace-scoped collection of path-addressed text documents. Attached to a session via `resources: [{type: "memory_store", memory_store_id, access: "read_write"|"read_only", instructions}]` — **attach-at-creation only**, max **8 stores per session**, `instructions` capped at 4,096 chars. [VERIFIED from source: https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/memory]
- It's **mounted as a real directory** in the session sandbox at `/mnt/memory/<slugified-store-name>/`, exposed via `mount_path`. The agent uses ordinary file tools. Writes outside the mount go to container-local scratch and are lost. `access` is enforced at the filesystem level. A description of each mount is auto-injected into the system prompt. [VERIFIED from source: same]
- **Limits: 100 kB (~25k tokens) per memory, 2,000 memories per store.** Docs explicitly advise "many small focused files, not a few large ones." Hitting 2,000 makes new writes fail (both API and agent file writes). [VERIFIED from source: same]
- **Full CRUD REST API**: `POST/GET /v1/memory_stores`, `.../memories` (create/list/retrieve/update/delete), with `path_prefix` (must end in `/`, matches whole segments) and `depth` (0 or 1 only). [VERIFIED from source: same]
- **Optimistic concurrency** via `precondition: {type: "content_sha256", content_sha256: "..."}` on update. [VERIFIED from source: same]
- **Immutable audit trail**: every mutation creates a **memory version** (`memver_...`), retained ~30 days (recent versions always kept), surviving deletion of the parent memory. There's a **`POST .../memory_versions/{id}/redact`** endpoint explicitly positioned for "compliance workflows such as removing leaked secrets, PII, or user deletion requests" — i.e. a GDPR-erasure primitive. A version that is the current head cannot be redacted. There is **no restore endpoint**; you re-write the content. [VERIFIED from source: same]
- **Security warning worth quoting for a survey**: stores default to `read_write`, and "a successful prompt injection could write malicious content into the store. Later sessions then read that content as trusted memory." Docs recommend `read_only` for reference material. [VERIFIED from source: same]

### NEW in 2026 (c) — **Dreams** (Anthropic's consolidation/"sleep" pass)

Direct structural parallel to OpenAI's "dreaming," and to your repo's own consolidation job.

- Research preview announced **May 6, 2026**, gated by beta header **`dreaming-2026-04-21`** (dream endpoints need *both* `managed-agents-2026-04-01,dreaming-2026-04-21`). [VERIFIED from source: https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/release-notes/api and https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/dreams]
- Mechanism: an **async job** taking (1) one pre-existing memory store and (2) **1–100 past session transcripts**, producing a **brand-new output memory store** with "duplicates merged, stale or contradicted entries replaced with the latest value, and new insights surfaced." **The input store is never modified** — you review and discard if you don't like it. [VERIFIED from source: https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/dreams]
- `POST /v1/dreams` with `inputs[]` (`{type:"memory_store"}` + `{type:"sessions", session_ids:[...]}`), `model`, optional `instructions` (4,096 chars). Lifecycle: `pending` → `running` → `completed`/`failed`/`canceled`. `drm_...` IDs. Endpoints: retrieve, list, `/cancel`, `/archive`. Runtime "minutes to a few hours." Billed at standard token rates. [VERIFIED from source: same]
- Important nuance for anyone building this pattern: `instructions` steers **synthesis**, not editing — "imperative directives that target specific lines ('change sentence X to Y') generally produce no change." [VERIFIED from source: same]
- While running, `session_id` points at the underlying session so you can stream its events and watch it read/write. Supported models during preview: `claude-fable-5`, `claude-opus-4-8`, `claude-opus-4-7`, `claude-sonnet-5`, `claude-sonnet-4-6`. [VERIFIED from source: same]
- Also: webhooks now cover `memory_store.*` (3 event types) and `environment.*` (4 event types) lifecycle, as of **July 22, 2026**. [VERIFIED from source: https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/release-notes/api]

## 4. OpenAI Agents SDK sessions

**Python is far richer than TS. Python ships a first-party MongoDB session; TS does not.**

**Python** — `Session` protocol at `agents.memory.session.Session`, four methods: `async get_items(limit=None)`, `async add_items(items)`, `async pop_item()`, `async clear_session()`. [VERIFIED from source: https://openai.github.io/openai-agents-python/sessions/]

Implementations (exact import paths): [VERIFIED from source: same]
- `agents.memory.sqlite_session.SQLiteSession` — file-backed or in-memory
- `agents.memory.OpenAIConversationsSession` — server-managed via OpenAI's Conversations API
- `agents.memory.openai_responses_compaction_session.OpenAIResponsesCompactionSession` — auto or manual history compaction via Responses API
- `agents.extensions.memory.async_sqlite_session.AsyncSQLiteSession` (aiosqlite)
- `agents.extensions.memory.redis_session.RedisSession`
- `agents.extensions.memory.sqlalchemy_session.SQLAlchemySession`
- **`agents.extensions.memory.mongodb_session.MongoDBSession`** — "horizontally-scalable, multi-process session storage," monotonic sequence counters for ordering
- `agents.extensions.memory.dapr_session.DaprSession` — 30+ backends via Dapr sidecar
- `agents.extensions.memory.advanced_sqlite_session.AdvancedSQLiteSession` — conversation **branching** + usage analytics
- `agents.extensions.memory.encrypt_session.EncryptedSession` — transparent encryption wrapper over *any* session, with TTL expiry

**MongoDBSession specifics** (useful reference implementation for your `@repo/knowledge` layer): [VERIFIED from source: https://openai.github.io/openai-agents-python/ref/extensions/memory/mongodb_session/]
```python
MongoDBSession(session_id: str, *, client: AsyncMongoClient[Any],
               database: str = "agents",
               sessions_collection: str = "agent_sessions",
               messages_collection: str = "agent_messages",
               session_settings: SessionSettings | dict | None = None)
```
Two collections: `agent_sessions` (`session_id`, `created_at`, `updated_at`, `_seq` atomic counter) and `agent_messages` (`session_id`, `seq` monotonic int via atomic increment, `message_data` JSON). Indexes: unique on `session_id`; compound `(session_id, seq)`.

Config: `agents.memory.session_settings.SessionSettings` (`limit=None` → all items, `limit=N` → last N). `RunConfig` exposes `session_input_callback` (customize history/input merging) and `session_settings`. [VERIFIED from source: https://openai.github.io/openai-agents-python/sessions/]

**TypeScript/JS** — yes, sessions exist, but the backend story is much thinner. Exact interface: [VERIFIED from source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/openai/openai-agents-js/main/packages/agents-core/src/memory/session.ts]
```typescript
export interface Session {
  getSessionId(): Promise<string>;
  getItems(limit?: number): Promise<AgentInputItem[]>;
  prepareHistoryItemForModelInput?(item: AgentInputItem): AgentInputItem;
  preserveReasoningItemIdsForPersistence?(): boolean;
  addItems(items: AgentInputItem[]): Promise<void>;
  popItem(): Promise<AgentInputItem | undefined>;
  clearSession(): Promise<void>;
}
```
Built-in JS implementations: **`MemorySession`**, **`OpenAIConversationsSession`**, **`OpenAIResponsesCompactionSession`**, plus marker interfaces `SessionHistoryRewriteAwareSession` and `OpenAIResponsesCompactionAwareSession`. **No built-in SQLite, Postgres, Redis, or MongoDB session in JS — you implement `Session` yourself.** [VERIFIED from source: https://openai.github.io/openai-agents-js/guides/sessions/]

**Takeaway for a TS/Mongo stack:** the JS SDK's `Session` is a 4-method interface you'd implement against your existing Mongo collections in well under 100 lines; the Python `MongoDBSession` schema above is a good template.

## 5. CrewAI memory

**CrewAI has been rewritten. The short-term / long-term / entity / external split is gone.**

- Current docs: "a **unified memory system** — a single `Memory` class that replaces separate short-term, long-term, entity, and external memory types with one intelligent API." Legacy types are **removed and consolidated**, not deprecated-but-present. [VERIFIED from source: https://docs.crewai.com/en/concepts/memory]
- **Storage backend is LanceDB (default), at `./.crewai/memory`** or a custom path via the `storage` param. **Not ChromaDB, not SQLite** anymore. [VERIFIED from source: same]
- Organization is **hierarchical scopes — filesystem-like paths** such as `/project/alpha` or `/agent/researcher`, enabling retrieval scoped to a subtree. `MemoryScope` restricts to a subtree; `MemorySlice` combines disjoint scopes. [VERIFIED from source: same]
- API: `remember(content, scope=None, source=None, private=False, categories=None)`, `recall(query, limit=10, depth="deep", scope=None, source=None)`, `extract_memories(raw_text)` (splits unstructured text into atomic facts), plus `remember_many()`, `forget()`, `scope()`, `slice()`, `tree()`, `info()`, `reset()`. [VERIFIED from source: same]
- **Retrieval is composite-scored**: semantic similarity × recency decay × LLM-assigned importance. Two recall modes: **"shallow"** (~200ms pure vector search) and **"deep"** (multi-step retrieval with LLM analysis, used for queries >200 chars). [VERIFIED from source: same]
- An **LLM is in the loop at three points**: ingestion (infers scope, categories, importance), query processing (deep recall), and extraction. Default LLM `gpt-4o-mini`; lazy init so missing API keys don't blow up construction. [VERIFIED from source: same]
- **Automatic consolidation/dedup** at a **0.85 similarity threshold**; non-blocking background writes, with `recall()` awaiting pending writes. Source tracking + privacy flags for multi-user isolation. [VERIFIED from source: same]
- Embedders: OpenAI (default `text-embedding-3-large`), Ollama, Azure OpenAI, Google AI/Vertex, Cohere, VoyageAI, AWS Bedrock, Hugging Face, Jina, IBM WatsonX, or a custom callable. [VERIFIED from source: same]

Agents share the crew memory by default; `Agent(memory=memory.scope("/agent/researcher"))` gives a scoped view. The crew auto-extracts facts from task outputs and injects recalled context before each task. [VERIFIED from source: same]

### A0. "Knowledge Engine" is NOT a product. Definitively.

The premise in your brief is wrong, and I can prove it four ways:

1. **Discovery doc**: `aiplatform` v1beta1 rev 20260725 contains **zero** resources, methods, or schemas containing "knowledge". Only 5 unique prose occurrences exist, all generic (e.g. `Retrieval` = "Defines a retrieval tool that model can call to access external knowledge"). There are **no** `knowledgeBases`, `knowledgeEngine`, or `knowledgeCorpora` endpoints in v1 **or** v1beta1.
2. **No such API host**: `knowledgeengine.googleapis.com`, `ragengine.googleapis.com`, `knowledge.googleapis.com`, `agentretrieval.googleapis.com` all return 404 on `$discovery/rest`. The Google APIs discovery directory (523 APIs) has no Knowledge Engine entry.
3. **Official rename table** (Agent Platform release notes, **April 22, 2026**) says exactly: `Vertex AI RAG Engine` → **`RAG Engine`**. Nothing about Knowledge Engine.
4. **Where the confusion comes from**: two places.
   - ADK docs (`google.github.io/adk-docs/sessions/memory/` — note: **`adk.dev/docs/sessions/memory/` 404s**) contain a comparison table saying `VertexAiRagMemoryService` → Persistence: *"Yes, stored in Knowledge Engine"*, *"indexed by Knowledge Engine"*, *"Requires Knowledge Engine"*. But the constructor on the same page is still `VertexAiRagMemoryService(rag_corpus="projects/PROJECT_ID/locations/LOCATION/ragCorpora/CORPUS_ID", similarity_top_k=5, vector_distance_threshold=0.6)`. It is ADK doc prose only, unsupported by any API surface or GCP doc.
   - The corpus management page is titled **"Manage your RAG knowledge base (corpus)"** — "knowledge base" is used as a plain-English synonym for `RagCorpus`.

**Verdict: "Knowledge Engine" is ADK documentation drift, not a rename. The product is RAG Engine; the resource is `ragCorpora`.**

### A1. Substrate

Two mutually-exclusive, project-level **deployment modes** (this is entirely new since May 2026 and is the single biggest thing a stale model gets wrong):

| | **Serverless mode** | **Spanner mode** |
|---|---|---|
| Resource storage | Fully-managed serverless DB | Dedicated Spanner Enterprise instance in a Google-owned per-customer project |
| Default vector DB | **`RagManagedVertexVectorSearch`** (a Vector Search 2.0 / Agent Retrieval Collection provisioned **in your project**) | `RagManagedDb` (Spanner) |
| CMEK | **Not supported** | Supported |
| VPC-SC | Supported | Supported |
| Allowed vector DBs | Managed VS 2.0, Pinecone, Weaviate | RagManagedDb, Managed VS 2.0, VS 1.0, Pinecone, Weaviate |
| Cost | Free for orchestration; vector DB billed directly | Tier-priced Spanner |
| Status | **Preview, us-central1 only**, no allowlist | GA, default if unset |

Data is **strictly isolated between modes**; switching modes hides (never deletes/moves) the other mode's corpora. Only one active at a time. Controlled via `GetRagEngineConfig` / `UpdateRagEngineConfig` (project-level singleton `projects/{p}/locations/{l}/ragEngineConfig`).

`RagManagedDbConfig` oneof: `.spanner{.basic|.scaled|.unprovisioned}` | `.serverless` | `.enterprise` (v1beta1 only). **`.basic`, `.scaled`, `.unprovisioned` at the top level of `RagManagedDbConfig` are explicitly marked "Deprecated: Use `mode` instead to set the tier under Spanner."**

Spanner tier sizing (exact): **Basic = 100 processing units (0.1 node) fixed, with backup** (default). **Scaled = autoscaling min 1 node (1,000 PU) → max 10 nodes (10,000 PU), with backup.** **Unprovisioned = deletes the Spanner instance and ALL RAG data, unrecoverable, halts billing.**

### A2. Write path

```

PATCH .../ragCorpora/{id}                                               (patch; also triggers ANN rebuild)

POST  upload/v1beta1/.../ragCorpora/{id}/ragFiles:upload                (UploadRagFile, media)
DELETE .../ragCorpora/{id}/ragFiles/{fid}
```
v1beta1-only metadata plane (**Preview**, and **not supported in Serverless mode**):

POST/GET/PATCH/DELETE .../ragCorpora/{id}/ragFiles/{fid}/ragMetadata[:batchCreate|:batchDelete]
```
`RagDataSchema` types: `INTEGER | FLOAT | STRING | DATETIME | BOOLEAN | LIST` (value fields `int_value`, `float_value`, `str_value`, `datetime_value` RFC3339, `bool_value`, `list_value`).

`ImportRagFilesConfig` sources: `gcsSource`, `googleDriveSource`, `jiraSource`, `slackSource`, `sharePointSources`. Sinks: `importResultGcsSink`, `importResultBigquerySink` (the older `partialFailureGcsSink` / `partialFailureBigquerySink` are **Deprecated**). `ragFileMetadataConfig` is **"Deprecated: Not in use."**

### A8. `RagCorpus.corpusTypeConfig.memoryCorpus` — the memory-corpus path

```
RagCorpusCorpusTypeConfig {
  documentCorpus {}                       // empty message, no fields
  memoryCorpus { llmParser: RagFileParsingConfigLlmParser }
}
```
**Status: v1beta1 ONLY (the whole `corpusTypeConfig` / `CorpusTypeConfig` schema is absent from v1 GA), and the only doc covering it — "Use RAG Engine in Gemini Live API" — carries an `Experimental` banner (weaker than Preview).**

What it actually is: a corpus whose ingestion path is the **Gemini Live API session transcript**, not files. You set `VertexRagStore.storeContext = true` on the retrieval tool and Gemini auto-memorizes the client↔Gemini interaction into that corpus and retrieves from it on later turns, **including across different Live API sessions**. It stores/indexes **text and audio speech**. The `llmParser` is mandatory and is what turns raw session context into indexed memory (`llmParser.modelName` example in docs: `gemini-2.5-pro-preview-05-06`). Embedding models: "currently supports Google first-party embedding models" (e.g. `text-embedding-005`).

Assessment: this is a *thin, experimental* memory path — no scoping keys, no consolidation, no revisions, no TTL, no purge. It is not competitive with Memory Bank. If you want agent memory on GCP, Memory Bank is the real product (below).

## TOPIC A′ — Memory Bank (you didn't ask, but this is the actual agent-memory substrate and it changed enormously)

This is where a May-2026 model is most wrong.

**New: `memoryBanks` is a first-class URL collection in BOTH v1 (GA) and v1beta1.**
```
POST   v1/projects/{p}/locations/{l}/memoryBanks/{mbId}:ingestEvents
POST   .../memoryBanks/{mbId}/memories            (create)
POST   .../memoryBanks/{mbId}/memories:retrieve
POST   .../memoryBanks/{mbId}/memories:generate
POST   .../memoryBanks/{mbId}/memories:purge
POST   .../memoryBanks/{mbId}/memories:retrieveProfiles     (v1beta1 only)
POST   .../memoryBanks/{mbId}/memories/{mId}:rollback
GET    .../memoryBanks/{mbId}/memories/{mId}/revisions[/{rId}]
```
plus a **global (no project/location) alias**: `v1beta1/memoryBanks/{mbId}/memories:retrieve` etc.

⚠️ **Trap**: every parameter description under `memoryBanks/*` still says *"The resource name of the ReasoningEngine…  Format: `projects/{p}/locations/{l}/reasoningEngines/{reasoning_engine}`"*. And the docs create a Memory Bank via `client.agent_engines.create(...)`, returning a `reasoningEngines/...` name. So **`memoryBanks/{id}` is a URL alias over the same ReasoningEngine resource** — there is no `memoryBanks.create`/`.list`/`.delete`. Deleting the Agent Runtime instance deletes the memories.

- **Substrate**: managed; config lives at `ReasoningEngine.contextSpec.memoryBankConfig`.
- **Write**: `CreateMemory` (explicit), `GenerateMemories` (LLM extract+consolidate; sources = `vertexSessionSource` | `directContentsSource` | `directMemoriesSource` (≤ **5** pre-extracted facts); **request max size 8 MB**), `IngestEvents` (**GA July 8 2026**; streaming with `generationTriggerConfig.generationRule{eventCount, idleDuration, fixedInterval, overlapEventCount}`; **unflushed streams auto-flush 24 h after last event**).
- **Read**: `RetrieveMemories` with `similaritySearchParams{searchQuery, topK}` or `simpleRetrievalParams{pageSize,pageToken}` — **default 3, max 100, values >100 coerced to 100**. AIP-160 `filter` on `fact`/`create_time`/`update_time`/`topics`; `filterGroups` = disjunctive-normal-form metadata filters (OR of ANDs) with ops `EQUAL|GREATER_THAN|LESS_THAN` + `negate`. `RetrieveProfiles` returns low-latency structured profiles.
- **Granularity**: `Memory{fact, structuredContent{data, schemaId}, topics[], metadata{}, scope{}, ttl, expireTime}`. `memoryType ∈ {NATURAL_LANGUAGE_COLLECTION, STRUCTURED_PROFILE}`.
- **Scoping**: `scope` is a required immutable arbitrary string map (e.g. `{"user_id":"123","agent_name":"x"}`). Retrieval requires **exact** key+value match (case-sensitive, order-insensitive). Wildcard `*` forbidden in values.
- **Consolidation/dedup**: LLM ADD/UPDATE/DELETE against existing same-scope memories. `consolidationConfig.revisionsPerCandidateCount` (default **1**) controls how many prior revisions the consolidator inspects. `disableConsolidation`, `metadataMergeStrategy ∈ {OVERWRITE, MERGE, REQUIRE_EXACT_MATCH}`. Managed topics: `USER_PERSONAL_INFO | USER_PREFERENCES | KEY_CONVERSATION_DETAILS | EXPLICIT_INSTRUCTIONS`; plus `customMemoryTopic{label, description}` and `generateMemoriesExamples` few-shots; `enableThirdPersonMemories` (default false = first person); `disableNaturalLanguageMemories`.
- **Versioning/audit/deletion**: **`MemoryRevision`** immutable snapshots with `extractedMemories[]{fact, structuredData, context}` showing pre-consolidation extraction. `:rollback{targetRevisionId}`. **Default revision TTL 365 days** (`memoryRevisionDefaultTtl`). After parent memory deletion, revisions remain inspectable/recoverable for **48 hours**. `disableMemoryRevisions` at instance or request level. `PurgeMemories{filter, filterGroups, force}` — `force=false` validates only.
- **Defaults changed**: generation model is **`gemini-3.5-flash` effective June 29, 2026** (was `gemini-2.5-flash`; instances created before that date keep 2.5-flash). Embedding default `text-embedding-005`; **`gemini-embedding-2` supported since July 8, 2026 but ONLY with `global`, `us`, or `eu` in the model resource name — regional (`us-central1`) is rejected.**
- **Regions**: 23 single regions + **multi-region `us`/`eu` and `global` (GA June 17, 2026)**. Memory Bank specifically **not** supported in `asia-southeast2`, `australia-southeast2`, `northamerica-northeast2`. **CMEK is impossible on the `global` endpoint.**
- **IAM**: scope-level IAM Conditions via API attribute **`aiplatform.googleapis.com/memoryScope`** in CEL, e.g. `api.getAttribute('aiplatform.googleapis.com/memoryScope', {})['userId'] == 'userA'`. Specialized roles **`roles/aiplatform.memoryViewer` / `memoryEditor` / `memoryUser`**. Limits: **1,500 unique principals per IAM policy**; conditions **not supported on multi-scope methods**. Docs warn to prefer positive conditions (empty scope matches negative conditions overly broadly).
- **Pricing (effective September 1, 2026)**: Storage **$0.30/GiB-month** (Agent Storage, *includes revisions*); Reads **1 Agent Compute vCPU-h ($0.085) per 3,000,000 read ops**; Writes **$0.085 per 1,000,000 write ops**; generation + embedding tokens billed separately at model SKUs. Sessions is priced identically.
- **Prompt injection**: docs explicitly name **memory poisoning** as a risk and recommend **Model Armor**, adversarial testing/red teaming, and sandboxed execution.

## TOPIC B — Agent Retrieval (formerly Vector Search 2.0)

**It is a separate API on its own host — this is the single most important structural fact.**

`https://vectorsearch.googleapis.com/` — "Vector Search API", rev **20260723**, versions **v1alpha / v1beta / v1** all present. Python client: `google.cloud.vectorsearch_v1beta`, `VectorSearchServiceClient`. gcloud surface: `gcloud vector-search collections create`. P4 SA: `service-{PROJECT_NUMBER}@gcp-sa-vectorsearch.iam.gserviceaccount.com`.

Resource model replaces "index-as-a-service" with **Collections of Data Objects**:
```
v1beta/projects/{p}/locations/{l}/collections                      POST/GET
       .../collections/{c}                                         GET/PATCH/DELETE
       .../collections/{c}:importDataObjects   :exportDataObjects
       .../collections/{c}/dataObjects                             POST/GET/PATCH/DELETE
       .../collections/{c}/dataObjects:batchCreate :batchUpdate :batchDelete
       .../collections/{c}/dataObjects:search  :batchSearch  :query  :aggregate
       .../collections/{c}/indexes                                 POST/GET/PATCH/DELETE
```
- **Write**: `DataObject{ name, dataObjectId (1–63 chars, RFC1035), data{}, vectors{}, etag }` — **optimistic concurrency via `etag`**. Collection has `dataSchema` (**JSON Schema Draft‑7**) + `vectorSchema`.
- **Auto-embedding**: `DenseVectorField{ dimensions, vertexEmbeddingConfig{ modelId, taskType, textTemplate } }` where `textTemplate` interpolates data fields (`"Movie Title: {title} ---- Movie Plot: {plot}"`). `taskType ∈ RETRIEVAL_QUERY | RETRIEVAL_DOCUMENT | SEMANTIC_SIMILARITY | CLASSIFICATION | CLUSTERING | QUESTION_ANSWERING | FACT_VERIFICATION | CODE_RETRIEVAL_QUERY`. Auto-embedding calls `aiplatform.googleapis.com` and burns *both* quotas.
- **Read**: `:search` with oneof `semanticSearch{searchText, searchField, taskType, topK, filter, outputFields, searchHint}` | `vectorSearch{searchField, vector|sparseVector, topK, distanceMetric, filter}` | `textSearch{searchText, dataFieldNames[], topK}`. Filters are **MongoDB-style JSON structs**: `{"genre": {"$eq": "sci-fi"}}`. `:batchSearch` fuses sub-searches via `Ranker{ rrf{weights[]} | vertexRanker{model, topN, textRecordSpec} }` — **`vertexRanker.model` currently supports only `semantic-ranker-fast@latest`**. `pageSize` max **1000** (KNN only). `:query` = metadata-only filter query, default page 100, max 1000.
- **Indexes**: `Index{ indexField, denseScann{featureNormType: NONE|UNIT_L2_NORM}, filterFields[], storeFields[], distanceMetric: DOT_PRODUCT(default)|COSINE_DISTANCE, dedicatedInfrastructure{mode: STORAGE_OPTIMIZED|PERFORMANCE_OPTIMIZED, autoscalingSpec{minReplicaCount default 2, ≥1 ≤1000; maxReplicaCount ≤1000, v1beta default max(min,5)}} }`. A Collection can hold multiple indexes (one per vector field). `searchHint` lets you force index vs KNN; default = use index if present, else fall back to KNN.
- **VS 1.0 migration**: `ImportDataObjects` with flag **`detect_and_convert_vs1_json`**; `restricts` → `data.restricts` + `data.restricts_deny`; `numeric_restricts` → `data.numeric_restricts`; `embedding`→`vectors.embedding.dense_vector`, `sparse_embedding`→`vectors.sparse_embedding.sparse_vector` (`dimensions`→`indices`).
- **Regions (9)**: asia-east1, asia-northeast1, asia-southeast1, europe-north1, europe-west2, europe-west4, us-central1, us-east4, us-west1.
- **CMEK**: `encryptionSpec.cryptoKeyName`, KMS key must be **same region**, **immutable — cannot be enabled on an existing Collection** (must export → new Collection → import). **No manual or automatic re-encryption/rewrap.** Keep old key versions ≥30 days. **VPC-SC supported.**
- **Quotas** are all metric-named `vectorsearch.googleapis.com/<metric>`, sliding-window per calendar minute, **429 `RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED` with `reason="RATE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED"` and the metric in `quota_metric`**. Metrics: control-plane `collection_management_requests`, `collection_read_requests`, `collection_list_requests`, `index_management_requests`, `index_read_requests`, `index_list_requests`, `lro_requests`; data-plane (per project/region/**per Collection**) `data_object_writes`, `data_object_reads`, `query_requests`, `search_requests` (ANN dense/sparse **and** text/semantic), `knn_search_requests` (exhaustive KNN), `batch_search_requests` (1 per call regardless of sub-searches, but sub-searches also count), `data_object_write_bytes`; allocation counts `collections`, `indexes`, `concurrent_index_operations`, `concurrent_collection_operations`, `concurrent_data_object_imports`, `concurrent_data_object_exports`. **Google does not publish the numeric default values on this page** — only the metric taxonomy.
- **Pricing (exact)**: Index Serving CUs — **Storage-Optimized CU $2.30/hour (includes 1 TB SSD)**; **Performance-Optimized CU $0.065/hour (includes 2 GB RAM)**; **Data Write/Update $0.45/GiB** (incl. initial build & full overwrite). Payload DB — **Data Stored $0.000410959/GiB-hour**; **Read ops $0.06 per 100,000**; **Write/Update/Delete ops $0.18 per 100,000**. Metering: a search = *Index Scan Cost* (1 read per batch of **up to 100 data objects** in the index) **+** *Document Retrieval Cost* (1 read per document returned). Direct read = 1 doc = 1 read. 1 doc = 1 write. Embedding model billed separately.
- **Status**: the API is `v1beta` in all doc samples; the docs still headline "Agent Retrieval (formerly Vector Search 2.0)". Vector Search 1.0 continues to exist separately (its own quotas: 5 concurrent index creates, 5 concurrent updates, 50 deployed index nodes, 5 N2D nodes, 100 indexes, 6,000 streaming update RPM; $3.00/GiB index build, $0.45/GiB streaming insert, per-node-hour serving).

**Relevance to agent memory**: it is the *default* embedding store behind RAG Engine Serverless mode (`ragManagedVertexVectorSearch`), so it is now indirectly the substrate under RAG-as-memory. It has no memory semantics of its own (no scope, no consolidation, no TTL) — it's a vector+payload DB.

There is also a **new `ces` v1beta — "Gemini Enterprise for Customer Experience API"**, plus `agentidentity` v1alpha, `agentidentitycredentials` v1alpha, `agentregistry` v1alpha, `developerknowledge` v1alpha in the directory.

### Does Gemini Enterprise offer end-user agent memory/personalization primitives?

**Yes — a fully productized, console-driven one, named "Personalization and Memory."** It is *not* Memory Bank and has no public API surface; it is end-user/admin UI.

- **Personalization** GA **July 31, 2025**. **"Save information as memories"** shipped **November 21, 2025**.
- Doc: `gemini/enterprise/docs/configure-personalization` — "Configure personalization and memory".
- Mechanics: Gemini Enterprise builds a **personal Memory** from (a) an explicit **user personalization profile** (Preferred name, role/job title, industry), (b) **Conversation history** toggle, (c) **connected data sources** (Microsoft Outlook, Microsoft OneDrive, etc. — extracts insights from email/calendar/docs), (d) **saved memories** created conversationally.
- Write path: user says *"Remember that all new proposals for Project Walby should be reviewed by @Roberto Moreno"* → agent replies *"I created a new memory: …"*. Update by restating. 
- Read path: `Settings > Personalization > Reference saved memories` toggle gates whether saved memories are injected into conversations.
- Delete: conversational (*"Forget my memory about X"*, *"Remove from memory"*) or `Settings > Personalization > Managed saved memories > Manage` → per-item delete or **Delete all**.
- **Admin controls**: `Gemini Enterprise app > Configurations > Feature Management > Memory and customization` toggle disables memory + personalization profiles **for all users org-wide**. **On by default.** Admins also control which data sources may be connected.
- **Known caveats stated in the docs**: data-source changes take **up to 24 hours** to take effect; **"The core memory feature is enabled by default. You can't disable the memory feature"** (end-users can only opt out of sources/saved-memory reference); **deleting a saved memory may not remove the information if the originating conversation is still saved — you must delete the conversation too.**
- Separate, older API-level primitive: **"Personalize responses from the answer method"** — GA **February 27, 2025** — pass user info on `answer` calls (`gemini/enterprise/docs/answer`).
- Security surface: dedicated `cmek`, `use-vpc-service-controls`, `access-transparency`, `audit-logging`, `identity`/`identity-mapping`, `enable-model-armor`, `org-policy-custom-constraints` pages. Model Armor screens Gemini Enterprise / Notebook Enterprise prompts and responses.

## TOPIC A — RAG Engine

### A0. "Knowledge Engine" is NOT a product. Definitively.

The premise in your brief is wrong, and I can prove it four ways:

1. **Discovery doc**: `aiplatform` v1beta1 rev 20260725 contains **zero** resources, methods, or schemas containing "knowledge". Only 5 unique prose occurrences exist, all generic (e.g. `Retrieval` = "Defines a retrieval tool that model can call to access external knowledge"). There are **no** `knowledgeBases`, `knowledgeEngine`, or `knowledgeCorpora` endpoints in v1 **or** v1beta1.
2. **No such API host**: `knowledgeengine.googleapis.com`, `ragengine.googleapis.com`, `knowledge.googleapis.com`, `agentretrieval.googleapis.com` all return 404 on `$discovery/rest`. The Google APIs discovery directory (523 APIs) has no Knowledge Engine entry.
3. **Official rename table** (Agent Platform release notes, **April 22, 2026**) says exactly: `Vertex AI RAG Engine` → **`RAG Engine`**. Nothing about Knowledge Engine.
4. **Where the confusion comes from**: two places.
   - ADK docs (`google.github.io/adk-docs/sessions/memory/` — note: **`adk.dev/docs/sessions/memory/` 404s**) contain a comparison table saying `VertexAiRagMemoryService` → Persistence: *"Yes, stored in Knowledge Engine"*, *"indexed by Knowledge Engine"*, *"Requires Knowledge Engine"*. But the constructor on the same page is still `VertexAiRagMemoryService(rag_corpus="projects/PROJECT_ID/locations/LOCATION/ragCorpora/CORPUS_ID", similarity_top_k=5, vector_distance_threshold=0.6)`. It is ADK doc prose only, unsupported by any API surface or GCP doc.
   - The corpus management page is titled **"Manage your RAG knowledge base (corpus)"** — "knowledge base" is used as a plain-English synonym for `RagCorpus`.

**Verdict: "Knowledge Engine" is ADK documentation drift, not a rename. The product is RAG Engine; the resource is `ragCorpora`.**

### A1. Substrate

Two mutually-exclusive, project-level **deployment modes** (this is entirely new since May 2026 and is the single biggest thing a stale model gets wrong):

| | **Serverless mode** | **Spanner mode** |
|---|---|---|
| Resource storage | Fully-managed serverless DB | Dedicated Spanner Enterprise instance in a Google-owned per-customer project |
| Default vector DB | **`RagManagedVertexVectorSearch`** (a Vector Search 2.0 / Agent Retrieval Collection provisioned **in your project**) | `RagManagedDb` (Spanner) |
| CMEK | **Not supported** | Supported |
| VPC-SC | Supported | Supported |
| Allowed vector DBs | Managed VS 2.0, Pinecone, Weaviate | RagManagedDb, Managed VS 2.0, VS 1.0, Pinecone, Weaviate |
| Cost | Free for orchestration; vector DB billed directly | Tier-priced Spanner |
| Status | **Preview, us-central1 only**, no allowlist | GA, default if unset |

Data is **strictly isolated between modes**; switching modes hides (never deletes/moves) the other mode's corpora. Only one active at a time. Controlled via `GetRagEngineConfig` / `UpdateRagEngineConfig` (project-level singleton `projects/{p}/locations/{l}/ragEngineConfig`).

`RagManagedDbConfig` oneof: `.spanner{.basic|.scaled|.unprovisioned}` | `.serverless` | `.enterprise` (v1beta1 only). **`.basic`, `.scaled`, `.unprovisioned` at the top level of `RagManagedDbConfig` are explicitly marked "Deprecated: Use `mode` instead to set the tier under Spanner."**

Spanner tier sizing (exact): **Basic = 100 processing units (0.1 node) fixed, with backup** (default). **Scaled = autoscaling min 1 node (1,000 PU) → max 10 nodes (10,000 PU), with backup.** **Unprovisioned = deletes the Spanner instance and ALL RAG data, unrecoverable, halts billing.**

### A8. `RagCorpus.corpusTypeConfig.memoryCorpus` — the memory-corpus path

```
RagCorpusCorpusTypeConfig {
  documentCorpus {}                       // empty message, no fields
  memoryCorpus { llmParser: RagFileParsingConfigLlmParser }
}
```
**Status: v1beta1 ONLY (the whole `corpusTypeConfig` / `CorpusTypeConfig` schema is absent from v1 GA), and the only doc covering it — "Use RAG Engine in Gemini Live API" — carries an `Experimental` banner (weaker than Preview).**

What it actually is: a corpus whose ingestion path is the **Gemini Live API session transcript**, not files. You set `VertexRagStore.storeContext = true` on the retrieval tool and Gemini auto-memorizes the client↔Gemini interaction into that corpus and retrieves from it on later turns, **including across different Live API sessions**. It stores/indexes **text and audio speech**. The `llmParser` is mandatory and is what turns raw session context into indexed memory (`llmParser.modelName` example in docs: `gemini-2.5-pro-preview-05-06`). Embedding models: "currently supports Google first-party embedding models" (e.g. `text-embedding-005`).

Assessment: this is a *thin, experimental* memory path — no scoping keys, no consolidation, no revisions, no TTL, no purge. It is not competitive with Memory Bank. If you want agent memory on GCP, Memory Bank is the real product (below).

## TOPIC A′ — Memory Bank (you didn't ask, but this is the actual agent-memory substrate and it changed enormously)

This is where a May-2026 model is most wrong.

**New: `memoryBanks` is a first-class URL collection in BOTH v1 (GA) and v1beta1.**
```
POST   v1/projects/{p}/locations/{l}/memoryBanks/{mbId}:ingestEvents
POST   .../memoryBanks/{mbId}/memories            (create)
POST   .../memoryBanks/{mbId}/memories:retrieve
POST   .../memoryBanks/{mbId}/memories:generate
POST   .../memoryBanks/{mbId}/memories:purge
POST   .../memoryBanks/{mbId}/memories:retrieveProfiles     (v1beta1 only)
POST   .../memoryBanks/{mbId}/memories/{mId}:rollback
GET    .../memoryBanks/{mbId}/memories/{mId}/revisions[/{rId}]
```
plus a **global (no project/location) alias**: `v1beta1/memoryBanks/{mbId}/memories:retrieve` etc.

⚠️ **Trap**: every parameter description under `memoryBanks/*` still says *"The resource name of the ReasoningEngine…  Format: `projects/{p}/locations/{l}/reasoningEngines/{reasoning_engine}`"*. And the docs create a Memory Bank via `client.agent_engines.create(...)`, returning a `reasoningEngines/...` name. So **`memoryBanks/{id}` is a URL alias over the same ReasoningEngine resource** — there is no `memoryBanks.create`/`.list`/`.delete`. Deleting the Agent Runtime instance deletes the memories.

- **Substrate**: managed; config lives at `ReasoningEngine.contextSpec.memoryBankConfig`.
- **Write**: `CreateMemory` (explicit), `GenerateMemories` (LLM extract+consolidate; sources = `vertexSessionSource` | `directContentsSource` | `directMemoriesSource` (≤ **5** pre-extracted facts); **request max size 8 MB**), `IngestEvents` (**GA July 8 2026**; streaming with `generationTriggerConfig.generationRule{eventCount, idleDuration, fixedInterval, overlapEventCount}`; **unflushed streams auto-flush 24 h after last event**).
- **Read**: `RetrieveMemories` with `similaritySearchParams{searchQuery, topK}` or `simpleRetrievalParams{pageSize,pageToken}` — **default 3, max 100, values >100 coerced to 100**. AIP-160 `filter` on `fact`/`create_time`/`update_time`/`topics`; `filterGroups` = disjunctive-normal-form metadata filters (OR of ANDs) with ops `EQUAL|GREATER_THAN|LESS_THAN` + `negate`. `RetrieveProfiles` returns low-latency structured profiles.
- **Granularity**: `Memory{fact, structuredContent{data, schemaId}, topics[], metadata{}, scope{}, ttl, expireTime}`. `memoryType ∈ {NATURAL_LANGUAGE_COLLECTION, STRUCTURED_PROFILE}`.
- **Scoping**: `scope` is a required immutable arbitrary string map (e.g. `{"user_id":"123","agent_name":"x"}`). Retrieval requires **exact** key+value match (case-sensitive, order-insensitive). Wildcard `*` forbidden in values.
- **Consolidation/dedup**: LLM ADD/UPDATE/DELETE against existing same-scope memories. `consolidationConfig.revisionsPerCandidateCount` (default **1**) controls how many prior revisions the consolidator inspects. `disableConsolidation`, `metadataMergeStrategy ∈ {OVERWRITE, MERGE, REQUIRE_EXACT_MATCH}`. Managed topics: `USER_PERSONAL_INFO | USER_PREFERENCES | KEY_CONVERSATION_DETAILS | EXPLICIT_INSTRUCTIONS`; plus `customMemoryTopic{label, description}` and `generateMemoriesExamples` few-shots; `enableThirdPersonMemories` (default false = first person); `disableNaturalLanguageMemories`.
- **Versioning/audit/deletion**: **`MemoryRevision`** immutable snapshots with `extractedMemories[]{fact, structuredData, context}` showing pre-consolidation extraction. `:rollback{targetRevisionId}`. **Default revision TTL 365 days** (`memoryRevisionDefaultTtl`). After parent memory deletion, revisions remain inspectable/recoverable for **48 hours**. `disableMemoryRevisions` at instance or request level. `PurgeMemories{filter, filterGroups, force}` — `force=false` validates only.
- **Defaults changed**: generation model is **`gemini-3.5-flash` effective June 29, 2026** (was `gemini-2.5-flash`; instances created before that date keep 2.5-flash). Embedding default `text-embedding-005`; **`gemini-embedding-2` supported since July 8, 2026 but ONLY with `global`, `us`, or `eu` in the model resource name — regional (`us-central1`) is rejected.**
- **Regions**: 23 single regions + **multi-region `us`/`eu` and `global` (GA June 17, 2026)**. Memory Bank specifically **not** supported in `asia-southeast2`, `australia-southeast2`, `northamerica-northeast2`. **CMEK is impossible on the `global` endpoint.**
- **IAM**: scope-level IAM Conditions via API attribute **`aiplatform.googleapis.com/memoryScope`** in CEL, e.g. `api.getAttribute('aiplatform.googleapis.com/memoryScope', {})['userId'] == 'userA'`. Specialized roles **`roles/aiplatform.memoryViewer` / `memoryEditor` / `memoryUser`**. Limits: **1,500 unique principals per IAM policy**; conditions **not supported on multi-scope methods**. Docs warn to prefer positive conditions (empty scope matches negative conditions overly broadly).
- **Pricing (effective September 1, 2026)**: Storage **$0.30/GiB-month** (Agent Storage, *includes revisions*); Reads **1 Agent Compute vCPU-h ($0.085) per 3,000,000 read ops**; Writes **$0.085 per 1,000,000 write ops**; generation + embedding tokens billed separately at model SKUs. Sessions is priced identically.
- **Prompt injection**: docs explicitly name **memory poisoning** as a risk and recommend **Model Armor**, adversarial testing/red teaming, and sandboxed execution.

       .../collections/{c}/indexes                                 POST/GET/PATCH/DELETE
```
- **Write**: `DataObject{ name, dataObjectId (1–63 chars, RFC1035), data{}, vectors{}, etag }` — **optimistic concurrency via `etag`**. Collection has `dataSchema` (**JSON Schema Draft‑7**) + `vectorSchema`.
- **Auto-embedding**: `DenseVectorField{ dimensions, vertexEmbeddingConfig{ modelId, taskType, textTemplate } }` where `textTemplate` interpolates data fields (`"Movie Title: {title} ---- Movie Plot: {plot}"`). `taskType ∈ RETRIEVAL_QUERY | RETRIEVAL_DOCUMENT | SEMANTIC_SIMILARITY | CLASSIFICATION | CLUSTERING | QUESTION_ANSWERING | FACT_VERIFICATION | CODE_RETRIEVAL_QUERY`. Auto-embedding calls `aiplatform.googleapis.com` and burns *both* quotas.
- **Read**: `:search` with oneof `semanticSearch{searchText, searchField, taskType, topK, filter, outputFields, searchHint}` | `vectorSearch{searchField, vector|sparseVector, topK, distanceMetric, filter}` | `textSearch{searchText, dataFieldNames[], topK}`. Filters are **MongoDB-style JSON structs**: `{"genre": {"$eq": "sci-fi"}}`. `:batchSearch` fuses sub-searches via `Ranker{ rrf{weights[]} | vertexRanker{model, topN, textRecordSpec} }` — **`vertexRanker.model` currently supports only `semantic-ranker-fast@latest`**. `pageSize` max **1000** (KNN only). `:query` = metadata-only filter query, default page 100, max 1000.
- **Indexes**: `Index{ indexField, denseScann{featureNormType: NONE|UNIT_L2_NORM}, filterFields[], storeFields[], distanceMetric: DOT_PRODUCT(default)|COSINE_DISTANCE, dedicatedInfrastructure{mode: STORAGE_OPTIMIZED|PERFORMANCE_OPTIMIZED, autoscalingSpec{minReplicaCount default 2, ≥1 ≤1000; maxReplicaCount ≤1000, v1beta default max(min,5)}} }`. A Collection can hold multiple indexes (one per vector field). `searchHint` lets you force index vs KNN; default = use index if present, else fall back to KNN.
- **VS 1.0 migration**: `ImportDataObjects` with flag **`detect_and_convert_vs1_json`**; `restricts` → `data.restricts` + `data.restricts_deny`; `numeric_restricts` → `data.numeric_restricts`; `embedding`→`vectors.embedding.dense_vector`, `sparse_embedding`→`vectors.sparse_embedding.sparse_vector` (`dimensions`→`indices`).
- **Regions (9)**: asia-east1, asia-northeast1, asia-southeast1, europe-north1, europe-west2, europe-west4, us-central1, us-east4, us-west1.
- **CMEK**: `encryptionSpec.cryptoKeyName`, KMS key must be **same region**, **immutable — cannot be enabled on an existing Collection** (must export → new Collection → import). **No manual or automatic re-encryption/rewrap.** Keep old key versions ≥30 days. **VPC-SC supported.**
- **Quotas** are all metric-named `vectorsearch.googleapis.com/<metric>`, sliding-window per calendar minute, **429 `RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED` with `reason="RATE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED"` and the metric in `quota_metric`**. Metrics: control-plane `collection_management_requests`, `collection_read_requests`, `collection_list_requests`, `index_management_requests`, `index_read_requests`, `index_list_requests`, `lro_requests`; data-plane (per project/region/**per Collection**) `data_object_writes`, `data_object_reads`, `query_requests`, `search_requests` (ANN dense/sparse **and** text/semantic), `knn_search_requests` (exhaustive KNN), `batch_search_requests` (1 per call regardless of sub-searches, but sub-searches also count), `data_object_write_bytes`; allocation counts `collections`, `indexes`, `concurrent_index_operations`, `concurrent_collection_operations`, `concurrent_data_object_imports`, `concurrent_data_object_exports`. **Google does not publish the numeric default values on this page** — only the metric taxonomy.
- **Pricing (exact)**: Index Serving CUs — **Storage-Optimized CU $2.30/hour (includes 1 TB SSD)**; **Performance-Optimized CU $0.065/hour (includes 2 GB RAM)**; **Data Write/Update $0.45/GiB** (incl. initial build & full overwrite). Payload DB — **Data Stored $0.000410959/GiB-hour**; **Read ops $0.06 per 100,000**; **Write/Update/Delete ops $0.18 per 100,000**. Metering: a search = *Index Scan Cost* (1 read per batch of **up to 100 data objects** in the index) **+** *Document Retrieval Cost* (1 read per document returned). Direct read = 1 doc = 1 read. 1 doc = 1 write. Embedding model billed separately.
- **Status**: the API is `v1beta` in all doc samples; the docs still headline "Agent Retrieval (formerly Vector Search 2.0)". Vector Search 1.0 continues to exist separately (its own quotas: 5 concurrent index creates, 5 concurrent updates, 50 deployed index nodes, 5 N2D nodes, 100 indexes, 6,000 streaming update RPM; $3.00/GiB index build, $0.45/GiB streaming insert, per-node-hour serving).

**Relevance to agent memory**: it is the *default* embedding store behind RAG Engine Serverless mode (`ragManagedVertexVectorSearch`), so it is now indirectly the substrate under RAG-as-memory. It has no memory semantics of its own (no scope, no consolidation, no TTL) — it's a vector+payload DB.

## TOPIC C — Google Agentspace → Gemini Enterprise

**Confirmed, with dates:**
- **October 9, 2025** — Gemini Enterprise release notes, Announcement: *"Gemini Enterprise: Google Agentspace is part of Gemini Enterprise. The Google Agentspace experience in the Google Cloud console and the default application is referred to as Gemini Enterprise. This includes all associated resources and documentation."*
- Doc host moved: `docs.cloud.google.com/agentspace/docs/*` **301 →** `/gemini/enterprise/docs/*`. `cloud.google.com/agentspace` 301 → `cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise`.
- **April 22, 2026** — separate, later event: Vertex AI folded into **Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform** (`docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/*`). These are two different fold-ins ~6 months apart; don't conflate them.
- Underlying API is still **`discoveryengine.googleapis.com`** (Discovery Engine API, v1alpha in the public directory). There is also a **new `ces` v1beta — "Gemini Enterprise for Customer Experience API"**, plus `agentidentity` v1alpha, `agentidentitycredentials` v1alpha, `agentregistry` v1alpha, `developerknowledge` v1alpha in the directory.
- Editions: **Standard, Plus, Frontline** (public docs) + **Business** (Help Center only). Standard/Plus bundle **Gemini Notebook Enterprise** (the renamed NotebookLM Enterprise).
- Concepts: data sources → **data stores** (one per entity type) → **apps** (= `engine` in the API; many-to-many with data stores = "blended search") → **assistant** → **actions** → **agents** → **analytics**.

### Does Gemini Enterprise offer end-user agent memory/personalization primitives?

**Yes — a fully productized, console-driven one, named "Personalization and Memory."** It is *not* Memory Bank and has no public API surface; it is end-user/admin UI.

- **Personalization** GA **July 31, 2025**. **"Save information as memories"** shipped **November 21, 2025**.
- Doc: `gemini/enterprise/docs/configure-personalization` — "Configure personalization and memory".
- Mechanics: Gemini Enterprise builds a **personal Memory** from (a) an explicit **user personalization profile** (Preferred name, role/job title, industry), (b) **Conversation history** toggle, (c) **connected data sources** (Microsoft Outlook, Microsoft OneDrive, etc. — extracts insights from email/calendar/docs), (d) **saved memories** created conversationally.
- Write path: user says *"Remember that all new proposals for Project Walby should be reviewed by @Roberto Moreno"* → agent replies *"I created a new memory: …"*. Update by restating. 
- Read path: `Settings > Personalization > Reference saved memories` toggle gates whether saved memories are injected into conversations.
- Delete: conversational (*"Forget my memory about X"*, *"Remove from memory"*) or `Settings > Personalization > Managed saved memories > Manage` → per-item delete or **Delete all**.
- **Admin controls**: `Gemini Enterprise app > Configurations > Feature Management > Memory and customization` toggle disables memory + personalization profiles **for all users org-wide**. **On by default.** Admins also control which data sources may be connected.
- **Known caveats stated in the docs**: data-source changes take **up to 24 hours** to take effect; **"The core memory feature is enabled by default. You can't disable the memory feature"** (end-users can only opt out of sources/saved-memory reference); **deleting a saved memory may not remove the information if the originating conversation is still saved — you must delete the conversation too.**
- Separate, older API-level primitive: **"Personalize responses from the answer method"** — GA **February 27, 2025** — pass user info on `answer` calls (`gemini/enterprise/docs/answer`).
- Security surface: dedicated `cmek`, `use-vpc-service-controls`, `access-transparency`, `audit-logging`, `identity`/`identity-mapping`, `enable-model-armor`, `org-policy-custom-constraints` pages. Model Armor screens Gemini Enterprise / Notebook Enterprise prompts and responses.
